therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Blocking androgen receptor signaling in prostate cancer cells
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Men with biochemically relapsed hormone sensitive prostate cancer
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy - Prostate (FACT-P) Total Score at 12 months

results.effect_size: FACT-P change at 12 months: LHRHa -8.04, Apalutamide -6.60, LHRHa + Apalutamide -9.42
results.target_engagement_evidence: DHT levels: Apalutamide increased DHT (+0.93 nmol/L at cycle 6, +0.86 nmol/L at cycle 12) while LHRHa decreased DHT (-0.90 nmol/L). Estradiol levels: Apalutamide increased estradiol (+87.87 pmol/L at cycle 6, +81.29 pmol/L at cycle 12) while LHRHa decreased estradiol
biomarker_changes: Testosterone recovery >150 ng/dL: median 23.33 months (LHRHa), 23.98 months (combination)
DHT levels increased with Apalutamide monotherapy, decreased with LHRHa
Estradiol levels increased with Apalutamide monotherapy, decreased with LHRHa
subgroup_findings: Participants without PSA/radiographic progression with testosterone recovery: 19.2% (LHRHa), 37.0% (Apalutamide), 37.9% (combination)
Time to PSA progression: 30.88 months (LHRHa), 25.79 months (Apalutamide), 36.11 months (combination)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events included acute myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia, transient ischemic attack
Fatigue increased across all arms, most pronounced at 3 months
Cognitive functioning declined, particularly with Apalutamide-containing arms
Sexual function declined across all treatment arms
results.dose_information: ARN-509 (Apalutamide) dose not specified in provided data

context.comparator: LHRH Agonist monotherapy vs Apalutamide monotherapy vs combination
